propositions: Seven decorated pytest fixtures copy complete os.environ into subprocess mappings and return them directly or nested in rendered arguments, exposing arbitrary inherited ambient secrets when pytest long traceback renders fixture arguments on unrelated assertion failures.

When pytest long traceback renders fixture locals via saferepr, inherited ambient credentials and sentinel values embedded in the os.environ copy become visible in test output, while short traceback does not expose them.

Each of the seven fixtures (materialize_probe, fetch_secrets, disk_pressure, health_gate, signals_gerrit_config, observability_exit, cli) must be replaced with an explicit allowlisted mutable mapping containing only fake-bin-first PATH plus required harness-specific variables.
All affected fixture consumers pass under a minimal parent environment (env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin), proving no behavioral dependency on arbitrary ambient inheritance.
Each fixture's allowlist must remain mutable to preserve existing per-test environment variable overrides while preventing disclosure of unrelated caller credentials.
A deterministic security oracle using insertion-ordered synthetic sentinels and unrelated failures must confirm no ambient credentials leak in long traceback output after the fix is applied.
